subject: Intermittent NFS/RPC timeouts after private cutover - packet drops & MTU suspicion
messages:
From: Srinivas Rao <srinivas.rao@northbridge.net>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+onprem@northbridge.net
Date: 2026-11-28T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private cutover - intermittent NFS/RPC timeouts

Hi Karthik,

We cut the private link over to Redwood's appliance in our DC-2 at 03:00 local this morning. Since then our application team is seeing intermittent I/O stalls hitting NFS mounts (tcp 2049) — periodic RPC timeouts that resolve after ~15-30s, then come back. We see the issue affecting database backups and some service healthchecks.

Initial facts:
- Errors spike around 09:00-11:00 PST and again late evening.
- Traceroutes attached (nb_traceroute_1128.txt) show the GRE/UDP tunnel via the partner edge.
- We captured a short pcap during a timeout (nb_onprem_pcap_1128.pcap).

We've already confirmed security groups allow 2049 and ephemeral ports, but the intermittent nature makes us suspect MTU/fragmentation across the encapsulated path or host offload behavior. Can you triage? This is impacting backups.

Thanks,
Srinivas Rao
Senior SRE, Northbridge Systems

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-28T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private cutover - intermittent NFS/RPC timeouts

Quick notes from initial pcap review (nb_onprem_pcap_1128.pcap):
- I see series of TCP segments for NFS with the DF bit set followed by retransmits and TCP fast-retransmit bursts.
- The path includes GRE/UDP encapsulation; inner packet sizes are occasionally ~1500B with outer headers pushing over the path MTU. Packets with DF set are dropped rather than fragmented.
- There are bursts where the MSS advertised from the server side is 1460, but the encapsulating path requires reduced MSS (~1360). No consistent MSS clamping seen on the PE.
- I also observed large send offload (TSO/GSO) signatures on the server-side capture that would create >1500 byte segments prior to offload. On an encapsulating path without MSS clamping that can cause drops.

Action items I'm executing now:
- Pull the host-level offload settings (ethtool -k) on the server VM host and ask SRE to disable GRO/TSO briefly for test.
- Request network team to apply MSS clamp policy on the GRE/UDP tunnel at the partner edge to 1360 and monitor.

Will upload tcpdump_flow_1129.pcap after the next window.

- Vanessa
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Srinivas Rao <srinivas.rao@northbridge.net>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-28T13:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private cutover - intermittent NFS/RPC timeouts

Srinivas — I asked your edge PO to confirm whether their firewall is performing any TCP MSS clamp or altering TCP options when translating traffic through the GRE/UDP tunnel. They replied this afternoon and attached a config diff showing no MSS clamp in place (attached as config_diff_fw.txt).

From our side we temporarily disabled GSO/TSO on the primary NFS host (vm-host-14) at 12:55 and immediately saw a reduction in retransmit bursts in the short window captured (tcpdump_flow_1129.pcap attached). Two observations:
- With offloads disabled, the server sends smaller segments that respect the encapsulated path’s MTU. Retransmits dropped by ~90% in the test window.
- However, disabling offload is not a long-term fix — it increases CPU. Correct fix is to ensure MSS clamp on the tunnel or reduce MTU on the server veth to pre-clamp size.

Can the Northbridge edge team apply MSS clamp to 1360 on the GRE/UDP tunnel? If they cannot, propose we set the VM network interface MTU to 1400 and configure graceful rollover.

-Marissa
PM, Hybrid Deployments, Redwood Inference

From: Srinivas Rao <srinivas.rao@northbridge.net>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-29T07:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private cutover - intermittent NFS/RPC timeouts

Thanks team — we applied an MSS clamp to 1360 on the partner-edge on 2026-11-29T07:20. Early telemetry: backups that previously failed are completing without RPC timeouts. We’re also keeping offloads disabled on a single host as a canary.

We have attached a follow-up pcap (tcpdump_flow_1129.pcap) showing no retransmit bursts during a backup window. Our ops will monitor for 24 hours and report anomalies.

We'll keep you posted, and we'll coordinate scheduling for a controlled MTU change on the rest of the NFS hosts if needed.

Srinivas

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-11-30T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Postmortem: NFS RPC timeouts post-private cutover (issue mitigated)

Summary:
- Impact: Intermittent NFS RPC timeouts and backup failures for Northbridge Systems after private cutover due to GRE/UDP encapsulation causing MTU oversize and drops for packets with DF set.
- Root cause: Encapsulated path reduced effective MTU; server-side large segment offload (TSO/GSO) produced oversized packets and the partner edge did not clamp MSS. Dropped packets triggered TCP retransmits and RPC timeouts.
- Immediate mitigation: Partner applied MSS clamp to 1360 on the GRE/UDP tunnel (2026-11-29 07:20 PST). We also disabled TSO/GSO on an affected host as a canary which reduced retransmits.
- Permanent remediation: (1) Implement MSS clamp policy on all GRE/UDP tunnels; (2) Add MTU validation in our private deployment checklist and automated validator during cutovers; (3) Add an ops playbook step to check/disable offloads temporarily during testing; (4) Document recommended MTU/MSS settings in the customer onboarding runbook.

Action owners / timelines:
- Network (Vanessa): Enforce MSS clamp in partner templates and add automated check — ETA 2026-12-08.
- Infra (Marissa): Add offload-checker and optional MTU adjust script in private deployment toolchain — ETA 2026-12-05.
- Customer ops (Northbridge): Gradual MTU standardization on hosts or confirm permanent MSS clamp — monitoring ongoing, report due 2026-12-01.

Thanks to the on-call infra and SRE teams for the quick turnaround. Closing ticket JIRA-NET-4521 after 48h of clean telemetry unless Northbridge requests further follow-up.

-karthik
Network Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
